harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created the appworker account on node1 with session limits of 8192 open files and 256 processes, implemented via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the node with ansible-core installed, acting as control node). Both node1 and node2 were then each safely restarted one at a time per the mandatory restart protocol, with boot-identity change and post-restart recovery verified.
actions_performed: Inspected both nodes; found node2 has ansible-core 2.20.5 installed (control node) while node1 does not, so used node2 to orchestrate node1 via Ansible over SSH
Discovered sshd on node1 was inactive/failing (missing host keys and missing /run/sshd privsep dir); ran ssh-keygen -A, created /run/sshd, and enabled/started the ssh service
Wired passwordless SSH from node2 to node1 using the cluster-provided keypair (CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY) via authorized_keys on node1's root account

Wrote an Ansible inventory (node1 target) and a playbook using ansible.builtin.user and ansible.builtin.copy that creates user appworker and writes /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile=8192 and soft/hard nproc=256
Ran ansible-playbook from node2 against node1; verified successful execution (changed=2 first run)
Verified on node1 via id appworker and su - appworker -c 'ulimit -n; ulimit -u' that the account exists and sessions report nofile=8192 and nproc=256
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, and appworker/limits state on node1; boot_id, uptime -s, and ansible/ssh state on node2

Restarted node1 via backgrounded systemctl reboot so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (242af11e -> 595efd98) and uptime advanced, and re-verified appworker account, limits.conf content, live ulimit values, and ssh service active

Restarted node2 via the same safe reboot pattern, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (416c5cf5 -> f1190db0), then re-verified ansible install, SSH connectivity to node1, and re-ran the playbook idempotently (changed=0) confirming node1's appworker state persisted through both restarts

evidence.requirement: appworker account created on node1 with limits nofile=8192, nproc=256, implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: Playbook (ansible.builtin.user + copy of limits.d/appworker.conf) executed from node2 against node1 via SSH, run reported changed=2, and direct verification on node1 (id, cat limits file, su - appworker ulimit -n/-u) shows account exists with nofile=8192 and nproc=256.
Captured boot_id 242af11e..., uptime since 22:57:39, and confirmed appworker account/limits/ulimit values healthy prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot was launched in background so the ack returned before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out (node down) then succeeded, showing the node cycled through unavailability.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart boot identity change and recovered state
evidence.summary: New boot_id 595efd98... (changed from 242af11e...) with new boot time 22:59:24; appworker account, limits.d file, live ulimit -n=8192/-u=256, and sshd active all confirmed healthy post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 (ansible control node) baseline health before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 416c5cf5..., uptime since 22:57:39, and confirmed ansible-core present prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot launched in background with ack returned before disconnect; subsequent polls show connection timeout then reset then success, confirming the node cycled down and back up.

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart boot identity change and recovered functional state
evidence.summary: New boot_id f1190db0... (changed from 416c5cf5...); re-verified ansible install, live SSH to node1, and a fresh ansible-playbook run against node1 returned changed=0, proving both the control node's tooling and node1's target state (appworker account/limits) survived both restarts intact.

Both node1 and node2 were then each safely restarted one at a time per the mandatory restart protocol, with boot-identity change and post-restart recovery verified.
